findings.problem: The scene reads as a vertical list of six equations (prime p, prime q, n = 5 x 11, z = (5 - 1) x (11 - 1), e = 3 + a tick, d = 27 + a check line), which is the 'could be replaced by a bullet list' failure. The one picture that is meant to show WHY n and z are what they are (the 5 x 11 cell grid, whose inner 4 x 10 block is z) is unreadable: 18 px cells with 3 px gaps (about 230 x 100 px), no labels for 5, 11, 4 or 10, and nothing says what the purple block means. The padlock and key pictograms, the whole point of the scene ('public key = lock, private key = key'), only arrive at 9.9 s, so for the first 9 s the right-hand 40% of the stage is empty and the scene is left-heavy.
findings.fix: Make the grid the hero of the scene: cells at least 24 px (11 columns x 24 + gaps is still under 300 px), a '5' label down its left side and an '11' label across its top at 28 px or more (blue, public), and when z lands label the purple inner block '4' and '10' and fade the dashed last row and column so the subtraction is seen as taking away a row and a column. Bring the pictograms in as the numbers are chosen instead of at the end: when n and e are published a blue padlock slides in beside them ('public'), when d is found a purple key appears beside it ('secret'), so the closing caption only confirms what is already on screen. Keep the arithmetic tags but treat them as labels on the picture.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s5-4.5.png (tiny unlabelled grid, empty right half), algo-8-s5-7.5.png (empty right 40% at 7.5 s), algo-8-s5-10.5.png (lock and key only now); scene-05-rsa-keys.js line 73 CELL = {size: 18, gap: 3}.

findings.problem: Caption 'Recompute every later hash and it looks valid again.' (8.2-10.8) runs ahead of its picture and states something the screen contradicts. The chain only looks valid at 10.75 s when the badge flips; for the first 2.5 s of the caption the picture shows a red cross on link 2-3, a red block 3 and the badge 'broken chain'. It also never says who recomputes the hashes: the forger (Eve) is not on screen, so a first-time learner does not know whose action this is.
findings.fix: Describe the action while it happens and put the payoff in the next caption: [8.2, 10.4, 'A forger recomputes each later hash to repair every link.'] then [10.8, 12.4, 'Now it looks valid again. Hashes spot edits, they do not stop them.'] (merge or drop the existing 11.0 caption so the badge 'valid chain' at 10.75 and 'but the edit is still there' carry the point).
findings.evidence: algo-8-s8-8.5.png and algo-8-s8-9.5.png (caption 'looks valid again', red cross, 'broken chain'), algo-8-s8-10.6.png (all ticks but badge still 'broken chain'), algo-8-s8-11.5.png (badge finally 'valid chain'); caps at scene-08-chain.js line 359.

findings.problem: Caption 'Each extra zero makes a hit 16 times rarer.' (8.8-11.0) runs ahead of its picture. During the whole caption the stage shows only a 16-square strip with 'starts with 0: 1 in 16'; the second zero ('starts with 00: 1 in 256') and the '16 times more work' sticker only appear at about 11.0-11.4, when the caption has already ended. At 8.8-9.8 the stage is nearly blank (a 6-square strip and one label).
findings.fix: Re-time the captions to the picture: [8.8, 10.9, 'One hash in 16 starts with 0.'] then [11.1, 13.3, 'Add a second zero: 1 in 256, so 16 times more work.'] (replacing the current 8.8 and 11.2 captions), or bring the 00 tag and the 256-cell grid forward to about 9.8.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s9-9.0.png (caption 'Each extra zero', empty stage), algo-8-s9-10.4.png (still only '1 in 16'), algo-8-s9-11.5.png (the 1-in-256 tag and '16 times more work' arrive); caps at scene-09-mining.js line 256.

findings.problem: The headline promises 'the same trick with numbers' but the mapping is never drawn. Nothing shows that g = 5 plays the role of the public gold paint, a and b the rose and blue secrets, or that A = 5^6 mod 23 is 'public paint + my secret'. The rule for the second half of the exchange ('raise what you received to your own secret') is also never said: at 8.0 the pills 19^6 mod 23 and 8^15 mod 23 just appear and the caption only reports the result ('Both get 2'). A learner who followed the paint scene cannot see which number is the 'mixture' and which is the 'second drop'.
findings.fix: Carry the paint colours across as small dots: a gold dot on the g tag (public paint), a rose dot on a = 6 and a blue dot on b = 15, and when A = 8 and B = 19 appear give them the orange and green mixture dots from scene 3. Say the rule in the caption at 8.0: 'Each raises what they received to their own secret: both get 2.' If space is short keep the dots and drop the longer 'secret numbers were never sent' wording (the purple secrets staying below the wire already shows that).
findings.evidence: algo-8-s4-1.5.png (p, g, a, b tags with no link to the paint), algo-8-s4-6.0.png (A = 8 and B = 19 are plain blue pills), algo-8-s4-8.5.png (19^6 and 8^15 with no stated rule).

findings.problem: The story never closes the loop to scene 2: the shared colour (scene 3) and the shared number 2 (scene 4) are never called the key. Scene 2 ends on 'how does Bob get the key without Eve seeing it?', but scene 3's caption says 'the very same colour' and scene 4's says 'Both get 2', so a first-time learner may not realise this value IS the cipher key (the 5 in 'key 5') or why they wanted it.
findings.fix: Make the payoff the answer to the question: scene 4 caption 8.0-10.2 'Both get 2: a shared key that was never sent.' and, after the equals sign pops at about 9.2, show a purple key icon with a '2' tag beside it (scene 3: a key icon beside the green equals disc and caption 'the very same colour: their shared key.').
findings.evidence: algo-8-s2-9.5.png (question 'how does Bob get the key'), algo-8-s3-9.5.png (caption 'the very same colour', no key), algo-8-s4-9.8.png ('Both get 2', no key).

findings.problem: Eve's hunt hits x = 6 (green tile, '6 tries') but her dashed purple 'a = ?' tag never resolves, so the toy break has no visible consequence: a first-time learner cannot tell whether the 6-try search worked or failed, and the contrast with the 617-digit number ('hopeless') is weaker. Green (valid/agreed) is also the colour of her success with nothing saying the toy exchange is broken.
findings.fix: At about 12.8-13.2 when x = 6 turns green, turn the ghost 'a = ?' into a solid red 'a = 6' with a small pop, so the toy secret visibly leaks; then '6 tries', the 617-digit number and the red 'no computer can search that' read as a clear before and after. Optionally recolour the hit red-on-light (Eve's colour) instead of green.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s4-12.2.png (five tries, 'a = ?'), algo-8-s4-13.5.png and algo-8-s4-14.7.png (x = 6 green, 'a = ?' still a ghost). Also raised in review-a8-facts.

findings.problem: The cipher step is not explained by the picture. The caption 'A cipher scrambles it with a secret key.' plays over six orange '+5' tags and tiles that flip in 0.35 s each; nothing says that '+5' means 'move each letter 5 along the alphabet' or that the key IS the 5. At 5.3 and 5.8 s the S to X change is a card-flip in motion, so the viewer never sees S and X side by side. A first-timer sees letters change and a number next to a key, but not the rule.
findings.fix: Change the caption to say it: 'A cipher shifts each letter 5 along. The key is 5.' and hold one finished pair for a beat (for example let the first tile stay as S above X with a small arrow and '+5' for about 0.6 s before the rest flip). Optionally add a tiny grey 'toy cipher' tag beside the row so it is not read as a strong cipher.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s2-5.0.png (one '+5' tag, letters unchanged), algo-8-s2-5.3.png (mid flip), algo-8-s2-6.2.png (all '+5', blue row, no rule); caption at scene-02-key-problem.js line 87.

findings.problem: 'Eve cannot unmix paint to find a secret.' (10.1-11.8) is drawn only as a red question mark between her two copies, which pops at 10.1-10.6 and then the scene fades. The key idea ('mixing is easy, unmixing is not') is asserted by the caption, not shown, and a learner can ask why Eve cannot simply add paint to what she holds.
findings.fix: Draw one attempt: from Eve's orange copy a red arrow back toward the three loose drops (gold, rose) ending in a red cross, or show her try to add a blue drop to the orange copy and get a brown that is not the tan (red cross on the colour mismatch). Keep the '?' as the end state and hold it a beat longer (it appears with under 1.5 s left before the fade).
findings.evidence: algo-8-s3-9.5.png (no sign of an attempt), algo-8-s3-11.8.png (just a '?' fading with the scene).

findings.problem: Two steps rely on jargon or magic the learner has not met. 'e = 3: it shares no factor with 40' ticks a green check with no demonstration, and 'factor' is only taught later (scene 6, 55 = 5 x 11). z = (5 - 1) x (11 - 1) appears as a formula with no reason to subtract 1. The learner cannot tell why e needs checking or why z must stay secret (only Bob knows 5 and 11).
findings.fix: Keep it short and visual: under 'e = 3' show the two factor lists (3: 1, 3 and 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40) with only 1 in common ringed in green, or reword the caption to 'Pick e = 3: only 1 divides both 3 and 40.'; at the z step add a small purple lock label 'only Bob can work this out' (he alone knows 5 and 11). Folds into the grid fix above.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s5-4.5.png (z formula with no reason), algo-8-s5-6.0.png (e = 3 'shares no factor with 40' tick).

findings.problem: Eve's attack skips the step that makes it work. The row reads '55 = 5 x 11' then 'so d = 27' with no z = 40 between them, so a learner who just watched scene 5 build d from z cannot see how knowing the factors gives the private key. The lower third is also the most crowded part of the video: nine pills (Eve's copies of the public key and 13, four trial divisions, '55 = 5 x 11', 'so d = 27', 'a real n: 617 digits') on two rows.
findings.fix: Insert a short pill between the two, 'z = 4 x 10 = 40', so the chain is factors, z, d (the three can sit on the second row and the '617 digits' tag can move to the stage's free right-hand area or appear after the row fades). Keep all labels at 28 px or more.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s6-9.6.png (55 = 5 x 11 alone), algo-8-s6-10.8.png (so d = 27 appears with no z), algo-8-s6-11.8.png (crowded final frame).

findings.problem: The scene's conclusion is implicit and rushed. 'A real n has 617 digits.' (10.4-12.0) is a blue 'public' pill beside Eve's red row with no consequence drawn, while scene 4's equivalent beat shows a red 'no computer can search that'. The learner must infer 'so factoring is hopeless'; the beat gets under 1.7 s and the scene fades right after. The same scene spends about 8 s on Alice's 7 -> 13 -> 7 arithmetic.
findings.fix: Make the caption carry the conclusion: 'A real n has 617 digits: nobody can factor that.' and add a red cross (or the 'no computer can search that' pill from scene 4) beside the 617-digit tag. If the beat needs more room, trim the 13^27 line's hold or start the Eve beat 0.5 s earlier.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s6-10.8.png and algo-8-s6-11.8.png (617-digit pill with no verdict), caps at scene-06-rsa-lock.js lines 181-182.

findings.problem: For about 1.3 s (about 4.4-5.7 s) the screen contradicts itself. Block 1 already shows the edited data and the new hash 9a1f8189, but the check row still says 'hash of block 1: fb28ccb9' (the OLD value, green digits), the link tick is green and the badge says 'valid chain', while the caption says 'Edit one block and its hash changes.' A first-time learner may read 'valid chain' as the result of the edit.
findings.fix: Reset the check row and badge when the edit starts: grey the row (or empty it) and swap the badge to a neutral 'checking...' (grey) at the moment the block's data changes, then let the new hash 9a1f8189 roll into the 'hash of block 1' slot just before the red cross at about 5.7, so the comparison always matches what the block shows.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s8-4.5.png and algo-8-s8-5.0.png (new hash in the block, old hash in the check row, green 'valid chain'), algo-8-s8-6.0.png (red cross appears).

findings.problem: The scene is top-heavy for most of its first half. Block 7 and the nonce list occupy only stage y 20-330; the lower half of the stage is empty from 0.5 to about 7 s (the 'find / check' bars arrive only at 7 s), and at 8.8-9.8 the whole stage is almost blank apart from a label and a 6-square strip. The figure is small for a video that is about watching hashes fail.
findings.fix: Centre or enlarge the mining figure: move block 7, its tag and the nonce list down about 100 px, or make the rows taller (84 px) with a larger digest font so the figure fills stage y 40-420, then keep the bars below it. Fade the first half out a beat before the strip grows so the second half does not start from a blank stage.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s9-1.5.png, algo-8-s9-4.5.png, algo-8-s9-6.0.png (everything above canvas y 600), algo-8-s9-9.0.png (nearly blank).

findings.problem: The three block cards sit flush against both stage edges (x 0-270, 333-603, 666-936; BLK = {y: 10, w: 270, step: 333}), so the house 12 px stage margin is broken and the cards jump when scene 8 hands over to scene 10 (scene 8's cards sit at about x 13-923). Block 1's border and Block 3's lip touch the stage boundary.
findings.fix: Use x0 = 12 and step = 321 (cards stay 270 wide, gaps 51 px, right edge at 924) and check that the link elbows and tick discs still fit the 51 px gaps; match scene 8's x positions so the handover looks continuous.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s10-1.5.png (cards flush with the stage edges), measured with a DOM scan: v-card x 0-270 and 666-936 in scene 10; scene-10-rewrite.js line 93.

findings.problem: Recap card 3 says 'Hashes link blocks, edits cost real work' but its pictogram only shows blocks 1-2-3 linked, block 3 flashing red and turning green (a chain repaired), so 'edits cost real work' has nothing on screen: no mining bar, no tries, no 0 seal. Proof of work is the last third of the video and the recap drops it.
findings.fix: Finish the pictogram with the work idea: after the three blocks go green add a short orange bar (or '50 tries' chip) under them, or give each block a small '0' seal chip that has to be re-earned, and keep the card text. The pictogram should still play once and hold.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s11-6.0.png (block 3 red, no work cue), algo-8-s11-8.5.png (final hold: only ticks and arrows).

findings.problem: 'Blockchain' is in the title card but is never named anywhere else on screen: scenes 8-10 are labelled 'HASH CHAIN' and 'PROOF OF WORK', and the recap says 'blocks'. The shift from secrets (scenes 2-6, Eve and the wire) to trust (scenes 7-10, no Eve) is also silent: scene 7 simply starts with the kicker 'HASH', so a first-time learner does not know why a fingerprint appears after RSA or that the second half answers a different question (how do we trust data?).
findings.fix: Name it where it first appears: scene 8 kicker 'BLOCKCHAIN: HASH CHAIN' (or add 'a blockchain' to the first caption) and recap card 3 'Chained hashes make a blockchain, edits cost real work'. Bridge in scene 7: kicker 'TRUST: HASH' and one early caption 'Next question: how do we know data was not changed?'
findings.evidence: algo-8-s7-0.5.png (kicker 'HASH', no bridge from scene 6), algo-8-s8-0.5.png (kicker 'HASH CHAIN'), grep for 'blockchain' in videos/a8 only hits the title card and comments.

findings.problem: Eve's red 'copy' arrow at 7.5-8.5 s starts at the wire's centre (x 468) but the blue row has slid to Bob's end (tile centres 522-842), so the arrow does not come from the letters it copies (in the first beat it did).
findings.fix: Start the arrow under the row (x about 680) and end it at Eve's copy row, or shift Eve's copy row to sit under it.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s2-7.5.png and algo-8-s2-8.5.png (arrow left of the blue row).

findings.problem: The video's red means Eve and broken, but Alice's literal secret paint is a saturated red (rose) that sits in a purple frame beside Eve's red-framed copies. It is a documented exception, yet at a glance the red pot at Alice's side can read as Eve's.
findings.fix: Shift the rose paint toward pink (more white-ish) or swap Alice's secret to purple-leaning magenta so the only saturated red on stage is Eve's.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s3-4.2.png and algo-8-s3-6.4.png (red secret pot next to red Eve).

findings.problem: The headline breaks as 'A hash is a / fingerprint of data', leaving the article hanging at the end of line 1.
findings.fix: Use ['A hash is a fingerprint', 'of your data'] (or ['A hash is a', 'fingerprint of data'] kept only if the break is intended).
findings.evidence: algo-8-s7-0.5.png.

findings.problem: Caption 'Edit block 1: its seal and the link both break.' (2.3-3.9) starts while the edit is still being typed ('ann pays EV' at 2.4 s) and the seal and link only break at about 3.0-3.4 s, so the caption leads its picture by roughly 0.7 s.
findings.fix: Start the caption at 2.8 (or 3.0) and end at 4.0.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s10-2.4.png (typing, all green) vs algo-8-s10-3.5.png (red cross and link broken).
